stem: In which city was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) born?
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) was born in Makkah, in the Arabian Peninsula, and received his mission there.

stem: What was the name of the father of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
explanation: His father was Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib, who passed away before the Prophet (PBUH) was born. Abdul Muttalib was his grandfather.

stem: What was the name of the mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
explanation: His mother was Aminah bint Wahb. Khadijah (RA) was his first wife, and Halimah was his foster mother.

stem: The year in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born is known as
options: the Year of Sorrow after the death of Khadijah (RA)
explanation: He was born in the year Abraha's elephant army marched against the Kaaba, so it is called the Year of the Elephant.

stem: Who took care of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) after the death of his mother?
options: His uncle Abu Lahab, a leader of the Quraysh
explanation: After his mother Aminah died, he was raised by his grandfather Abdul Muttalib, and then by his uncle Abu Talib.

stem: Who became the guardian of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) after Abdul Muttalib died?
explanation: Abu Talib, the father of Ali (RA), took charge of the Prophet (PBUH) and protected him later in Makkah as well.

stem: To which tribe did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) belong?
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) belonged to the Banu Hashim clan of Quraysh. Aws and Khazraj were the tribes of Madinah.

stem: Who was the foster mother who nursed the infant Prophet (PBUH) in the desert?
options: Aminah bint Wahb, his own mother
explanation: Infants of Makkah were often sent to nurse among desert tribes, and Halimah of Banu Sa'd cared for him. Umm Ayman was his attendant later.

stem: By which title was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) known among the Quraysh before prophethood?
options: Dhun-Nurayn, the Possessor of Two Lights
explanation: Even his opponents called him Al-Amin and As-Sadiq for his honesty. Al-Faruq was later the title of Umar (RA) and Siddiq of Abu Bakr (RA).

stem: Who was the first wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
explanation: He married Khadijah (RA) before the first revelation, and she remained his only wife until her death.

stem: What was the occupation of Khadijah (RA) when the Prophet (PBUH) married her?
options: A teacher of children in the city of Makkah
explanation: Khadijah (RA) was a respected businesswoman of Makkah who hired the honest Muhammad (PBUH) to take her goods to Syria.

stem: How did the Prophet (PBUH) settle the Quraysh dispute over who would place the Black Stone when the Kaaba was rebuilt?
options: He placed it on a cloth and let leaders of the clans lift it together, then set it in place himself
He asked the oldest man of Makkah to place it alone
He let the clans draw lots
He placed it alone without discussion
explanation: The Quraysh accepted his wise solution, which avoided bloodshed. Every clan shared in the honour.

stem: At about what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) receive the first revelation?
explanation: He received the first revelation at the age of forty in the Cave of Hira. At 63 he passed away.

stem: Who was the first person to believe in the message of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
explanation: Khadijah (RA) believed at once and comforted him after the first revelation. Others soon followed.

stem: Which companion of the Prophet (PBUH) is known as 'As-Siddiq'?
explanation: Abu Bakr (RA) was called As-Siddiq, the one who always confirmed the truth, especially after the Mi'raj.

stem: From which hill did the Prophet (PBUH) first publicly call the Quraysh to Islam?
explanation: After about three years of private invitation, he called the Quraysh from Mount Safa near the Kaaba.

stem: Which house in Makkah was used by the early Muslims as a meeting place for teaching?
explanation: The house of Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam near Safa was used for meetings. Dar an-Nadwa was the Quraysh council hall.

stem: Who is regarded as the first martyr in Islam, killed in Makkah for her faith?
explanation: Sumayyah (RA), mother of Ammar and wife of Yasir, was killed by the Quraysh because she would not give up her faith.

stem: Which companion, tortured by the Quraysh for refusing to give up Islam, later became the first caller to prayer (muadhdhin)?
explanation: Bilal (RA) endured being laid on hot sand and was freed by Abu Bakr (RA). He gave the first adhan in Madinah.

stem: To which land did a group of Muslims first migrate to escape persecution in Makkah?
explanation: In the fifth year of prophethood a group migrated to Abyssinia, where a just king gave them protection.

stem: By what title is the just Christian king of Abyssinia who gave refuge to the Muslims known?
explanation: The ruler of Abyssinia was the Negus, who sheltered the Muslims. Heraclius was the Byzantine emperor and Khosrau the Persian.

stem: Who spoke for the Muslims before the king of Abyssinia?
explanation: Ja'far (RA) explained Islam before the king and recited verses of Surah Maryam, which moved the Negus.

stem: Which companion, whose conversion strengthened the Muslims, was given the title 'Al-Faruq'?
explanation: Umar (RA) accepted Islam in Makkah, and his boldness gave courage to the Muslims. He was called Al-Faruq, the one who distinguishes truth from falsehood.

stem: For about how long did the Quraysh keep up their social boycott of the Banu Hashim in the valley of Abu Talib?
explanation: The boycott in Shi'b Abi Talib lasted about three years, until it was ended and the document was set aside.

stem: The 'Year of Sorrow' refers to the year in which the Prophet (PBUH) lost
explanation: Within a short time both his supportive wife Khadijah (RA) and his protecting uncle Abu Talib died, making it a time of great grief.

stem: Why did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) travel to Ta'if in the tenth year of prophethood?
options: To perform Hajj with the people of Ta'if
To trade with the merchants of Ta'if
To seek support for Islam, though the people treated him harshly
To fight the tribe of Thaqif
explanation: He went to invite the people of Ta'if to Islam after losing protection in Makkah, but they rejected him and drove him out with stones.

stem: What did Allah prescribe for the Muslims at the time of the Mi'raj?
explanation: The five daily prayers were enjoined during the Mi'raj, the Prophet's ascent through the heavens. Fasting, zakat and Hajj were prescribed later.

stem: In the Night Journey (Isra), the Prophet (PBUH) was taken from the Sacred Mosque in Makkah to
options: The Quba Mosque on the outskirts of Madinah
explanation: The Isra was the journey from Masjid al-Haram to Al-Aqsa, followed by the ascent (Mi'raj) through the heavens.

stem: The two Pledges of Aqabah were made with people from which city?
explanation: Believers from Yathrib met the Prophet (PBUH) at Aqabah near Mina and pledged to protect him, which prepared the Hijrah.

stem: Which companion was sent to Madinah as a teacher before the Hijrah to teach Islam to its people?
explanation: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) taught Quran and invited the people of Madinah to Islam, and many of the Aws and Khazraj accepted.

stem: In which year CE did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate from Makkah to Madinah?
explanation: The Hijrah took place in 622 CE and marks the first year of the Islamic calendar. 630 CE is the conquest of Makkah and 632 CE his death.

stem: Before the Hijrah, the city of Madinah was known as
explanation: Madinah was called Yathrib, and it became 'Madinat an-Nabi' (the city of the Prophet) after the Hijrah.

stem: In which cave did the Prophet (PBUH) and Abu Bakr (RA) take shelter on their way to Madinah?
explanation: They stayed three days in the Cave of Thawr to evade the Quraysh before moving towards Madinah.

stem: Who slept in the bed of the Prophet (PBUH) on the night of the Hijrah to mislead the Quraysh?
explanation: Ali (RA) lay in the Prophet's bed so the Quraysh would think he was still there. Abu Bakr (RA) travelled with the Prophet (PBUH).

stem: Which was the first mosque built by the Prophet (PBUH) after migrating?
explanation: He built the Mosque of Quba on the outskirts of Madinah on arriving. Masjid an-Nabawi was built after he settled in the city.

stem: Who started the Hijri calendar, with the year of the Hijrah as its first year?
explanation: The Hijri calendar was adopted in the caliphate of Umar (RA), who chose the Hijrah as the starting point.

stem: The Muslims of Madinah who welcomed and helped those who migrated are called
explanation: The helpers of Madinah are the Ansar. Those who migrated from Makkah are the Muhajirun.

stem: The pairing of each migrant (Muhajir) with a helper (Ansari) as brothers is known as
explanation: Mu'akhat means brotherhood, which helped settle the migrants and strengthened unity.

stem: The Charter of Madinah was an agreement that
options: ended the war between Madinah and Makkah for ever
set out the rights and duties of the Muslims, Jews and other tribes living in Madinah
explanation: The charter made the groups of Madinah a single community with a common defence and mutual obligations.

stem: Which companion hosted the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in his house on arrival in Madinah?
explanation: The Prophet's she-camel stopped near the house of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (RA), who hosted him until Masjid an-Nabawi and his rooms were built.

stem: In which year after the Hijrah was the Battle of Badr fought?
explanation: The Battle of Badr took place in Ramadan, 2 AH (624 CE). Uhud was in 3 AH and the Trench in 5 AH.

stem: Approximately how many Muslims fought in the Battle of Badr?
explanation: About 313 Muslims faced a force of around 1,000 from Makkah. The figures 700 and 3,000 belong to the armies at Uhud.

stem: What led to the early setback for the Muslims in the Battle of Uhud?
options: The Muslims ran out of water at the battlefield
A group of archers left their post on the hill
explanation: The archers left the pass after the Quraysh seemed to be retreating, and Khalid ibn al-Walid, then fighting for the Quraysh, attacked from behind.

stem: Which uncle of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was martyred in the Battle of Uhud?
explanation: Hamza (RA), known as the Lion of Allah, was martyred at Uhud. Abbas lived long after, and Abu Talib had died in Makkah.

stem: Who suggested digging a trench around Madinah in the Battle of the Trench?
explanation: Salman al-Farsi (RA) suggested the trench, a defence method known in Persia, and the Muslims dug it before the confederates arrived.

stem: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah established
options: the end of the Hijrah and return to Makkah
a ten-year truce between the Muslims and the Quraysh
explanation: The treaty in 6 AH set a truce, and the Muslims were to return the next year to perform Umrah. It later opened the way to peaceful spread of Islam.

stem: The pledge taken by the companions beneath a tree before the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah is called
explanation: Bay'at ar-Ridwan, the Pledge of Satisfaction, was mentioned by Allah in the Quran with approval.

stem: In which year after the Hijrah was the Battle of Khaybar fought?
explanation: Khaybar was fought in 7 AH, after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, against the fortresses north of Madinah.

stem: Who was appointed first commander of the Muslim army at the Battle of Mu'tah?
explanation: Zayd ibn Haritha (RA) was the first commander, followed by Ja'far and Abdullah ibn Rawahah. Khalid took over after they were martyred.

stem: The conquest of Makkah took place in which year after the Hijrah?
explanation: Makkah was conquered in Ramadan, 8 AH (630 CE), after the Quraysh broke the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

stem: How did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) treat the people of Makkah on its conquest?
explanation: He forgave those who had persecuted him for years, and most of Makkah then entered Islam.

stem: The Battle of Hunayn was fought soon after the conquest of Makkah against
explanation: Hunayn was fought in 8 AH against the tribes of Hawazin and Thaqif. The Byzantines were involved at Mu'tah and Tabuk.

stem: The expedition of Tabuk in 9 AH was undertaken because of
options: the threat of a Byzantine army on the northern border
a rebellion by the tribes in the far south of Yemen
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) marched towards the northern frontier after the news of the Byzantine army. It is also called the Expedition of Hardship.

stem: In which year after the Hijrah did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) perform the Farewell Pilgrimage?
explanation: The Farewell Pilgrimage was in 10 AH. He passed away a few months after it, in 11 AH.

stem: Which principle was stated in the Holy Prophet's (PBUH) Farewell Sermon?
options: No Arab has superiority over a non-Arab except by piety
The wealthy have greater rights than the poor in every matter
explanation: In the sermon at Arafat he declared the equality of all people, with superiority only in taqwa, and abolished interest and tribal vengeance.

stem: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) pass away?
explanation: He passed away at the age of 63, after 23 years of prophethood.

stem: Where was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) buried?
options: In the Cave of Hira on Jabal al-Nur
In the room of Aisha (RA) beside the Mosque in Madinah
explanation: He passed away in the house of Aisha (RA) and was buried in the same room. It is today inside Masjid an-Nabawi.

stem: In which year after the Hijrah did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) pass away?
explanation: He passed away in Rabi al-Awwal, 11 AH (632 CE). The Farewell Pilgrimage had been in 10 AH.

stem: For about how many years did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) call people to Islam in Makkah after the first revelation?
explanation: He preached in Makkah for about thirteen years and in Madinah for about ten, making twenty-three years.

stem: Which daughter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was married to Ali (RA)?
explanation: Fatimah (RA), the youngest daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and Khadijah (RA), married Ali (RA). Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum were each married to Uthman (RA).

stem: The son of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), Ibrahim, was born to which wife?
explanation: Ibrahim was born in Madinah to Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah (RA) and died in infancy. The other children of the Prophet (PBUH) were from Khadijah (RA).

stem: Which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was the daughter of Abu Bakr (RA)?
explanation: Aisha (RA) was the daughter of Abu Bakr (RA). Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of Umar (RA).

stem: Which widow did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) marry soon after the death of Khadijah (RA)?
explanation: Sawdah (RA) was the first wife after Khadijah (RA), then Aisha (RA). Zaynab bint Jahsh married the Prophet (PBUH) in Madinah.

stem: After the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, the Prophet (PBUH) sent letters to rulers. Which two empires were among those addressed?
options: The Chinese and the Japanese empires of the East
The Byzantine and the Persian empires
explanation: The letters invited rulers including Heraclius of the Byzantines and Khosrau of Persia. The other pairs were not among the rulers addressed.

stem: The mosque in Madinah where the direction of prayer was changed from Jerusalem towards the Kaaba is known as
explanation: Masjid al-Qiblatayn, 'the Mosque of the Two Qiblas', commemorates the change of direction during prayer.

stem: Which companion received the title 'Sayf Allah' (the Sword of Allah) from the Prophet (PBUH) at Mu'tah?
explanation: After the first three commanders were martyred, Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA) led the army, and the Prophet (PBUH) called him Sayf Allah.

stem: Which Qurayshi leader was killed in the Battle of Badr?
explanation: Abu Jahl was among the Quraysh leaders killed at Badr. Abu Lahab died in Makkah soon afterwards, and Abu Sufyan later embraced Islam.

stem: In seerah terminology, a 'ghazwah' is a military expedition
options: led only by Abu Bakr (RA) in the days of his caliphate
in which the Prophet (PBUH) himself took part
explanation: Ghazwah refers to campaigns in which the Prophet (PBUH) took part, as in Badr or Uhud. Those he sent others to lead are called sariyyah.

stem: The period of ignorance in Arabia before Islam is called
explanation: Jahiliyyah is the period before Islam, when idolatry and injustice were common.

stem: When the angel of the mountains offered to crush the people of Makkah between two mountains after the Ta'if incident, the Prophet (PBUH)
options: declined, hoping that their descendants would worship Allah alone
accepted at once without any hesitation
left the decision to Abu Bakr (RA)
explanation: He refused and said he hoped Allah would bring from them people who would worship Him alone. This shows his mercy (Bukhari and Muslim).

stem: At about the age of twelve, the Prophet (PBUH) travelled with Abu Talib on a trade journey to
explanation: He accompanied his uncle Abu Talib on a caravan to Syria, where the monk Bahira is reported to have noticed signs of his future prophethood.

stem: At which place between Makkah and Madinah did the mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) pass away?
explanation: Aminah died at Abwa on the way back from visiting Madinah, when the Prophet (PBUH) was about six years old.
